title: pool flap detection and heuristic sketch
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for reproducing and reasoning about a recurring scheduling/flap pattern in one of the Dedicated GPU pools (pool-id: gpu-dedicated-6). This is a working doc — notes, commands, raw outputs, hypotheses, and small experiments I want to keep in one place.

Summary of observed problem:
- Customer load shows repeated short ramps (~20–90s) causing the autoscaler to provision GPUs, then teardown shortly after. Net result: high warm-start churn, higher per-token cost and occasional request latency spikes when model loads collide.
- Pattern: request-rate derivative spikes (dR/dt) > ~40 rps/s, autoscaler scales up by 1-2 nodes (usually p4), pods schedule but model load time (TF/torch compile + KV warm) is 8–18s per replica. Before models warm, traffic falls and autoscaler tears down. Repeat across hours.

Recent timeline (UTC) — traced during customer incident on 2024-11-09:
- 03:12:05 request rate begins rising from 12 -> 55 rps over ~30s
- 03:12:35 HPA triggers scale-up target=3->5 replicas (policy: CPU/queue-proxy heuristics)
- 03:12:40 kube schedule logs: Pod gpu-svc-a -> node p4-12
- 03:12:46 container start, runtime log: "loading model v1.3 (quantized)"
- 03:12:57 runtime: "compiling kernels (fallback)" -> adds ~6s
- 03:13:06 runtime: "kv-cache warm start 0/64 prefixes"
- 03:13:30 external traffic drops to 18 rps (client backpressure)
- 03:13:40 autoscaler marks node underutilized -> drains -> pods evicted
- 03:13:58 kubelet error (on eviction): "failed to gracefully shutdown GPU context" (log snippet below)

Commands I ran (local devbox, kubecontext: prod-dedicated-6):
- kubectl get pod -n dedicated -l app=llm-svc -o wide --show-labels
- kubectl describe pod gpu-svc-a -n dedicated | sed -n '1,160p'
- kubectl logs gpu-svc-a -n dedicated --since=20m --tail=200
- grep -n "compiling kernels" /var/log/redwood/runtime/gpu-dedicated-6/*.log | tail -n 50
- curl -sS \"$MONITOR/api/traffic?pool=gpu-dedicated-6&window=60s\" | jq '.'

Representative error snippet from kubelet (raw):
"Nov  9 03:13:58 p4-12 kubelet[2134]: E1109 03:13:58.123 kubelet.go:2345] failed to stop container runtime for pod gpu-svc-a: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to kill process 8271: signal: killed. GPU fd stale, cleanup responded with EBUSY"

Runtime log excerpt (redacted):
"[03:12:46] INFO model_loader: loading weights /mnt/models/llama-q8/v1.3/part-0
[03:12:49] WARN perf: kernel cache miss - compiling cuda kernels (fallback path)
[03:12:55] INFO quant: apply q8x4 patterns -> 28ms
[03:12:57] INFO kvcache: warming 0/64 prefixes (concurrency=4)
[03:13:10] ERROR allocator: OOM while reserving scratch for fused-gemm -> falling back to slower matmul
[03:13:15] INFO runtime: ready for requests"

What I tried and the results:
- Increase warm_pool_size from 1 -> 2 for this pool in test stage (config flag warm_pool_target=2): reduced observed model load collisions, but increased baseline cost by ~12% and didn't prevent oscillation entirely.
- Set autoscaler.down_stabilization to 2m (was 30s): helped reduce teardown frequency, but increased time a cold node stays idle -> cost tradeoff.
- Disabled kernel fallback path (force AOT precompile at image build): eliminated the 5–8s compile bursts but made image build + deploy times heavier; still had warmup kv-cache time.
- Prototyped a small request-shepherding route: when new replica starts, a readiness gate delays routing until kvcache checkpoint applied and small health pings show <5ms per inference. This lowered tail latency but added complexity to routing / circuit-breakers.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Autoscaler sensitivity to short bursts: vertical sensitivity (scale count) reacts faster than warm models can start, creating feedback loops when bursts are bursty but shallow.
2) Kernel compile + kv-cache warm are the dominant fixed costs; any strategy that masks or amortizes those costs will reduce churn.
3) Clients implement retry/backoff patterns that amplify the problem: client-side retries increase instantaneous request rate, causing additional scale events.
4) Node preemption/drain semantics: when autoscaler tears down nodes without graceful GPU context cleanup we see failed stops that prolong evictions and increase instability.

Quick experiments to run next:
- Synthetic ramp test: use loadgen to generate triangular ramps with configurable slope. Measure dR/dt thresholds that cause scale events. Script: loadgen --slope 2 rps/s --max 80 --duration 120.
- Telemetry tweak: emit kernel-compile-start and kvcache-warm-complete events to monitoring with tags (pod, model, node) so we can graph distribution of warm times.
- Short-circuit: in the 0->N scale event path, pin one pre-warmed replica in cluster that can be checkpoint-restored in <4s using memory snapshot (experiment only).
- Eviction probe: trigger controlled drain on a test node and capture GPU driver logs to confirm EBUSY pattern.

Suggested heuristic (draft):
- Keep a minimum hot replica ratio Rhot = min(3, ceil(peak_rps / 40)). Rationale: observed single replica can safely handle ~40 rps before queuing raises latency.
- Use derivative-based scale-up: if dR/dt > X for 10s then prefer proactive scale-up by 2 replicas (X to calibrate via load tests).
- Increase down_stabilization window to 90–180s for these pools to avoid thrash on microbursts.
- Prefer node-level warm-pinning: when tearing down, prefer evicting nodes with the fewest warm models (score nodes by warm-ram & compile-cache hits).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How expensive is maintaining a persistent pre-warmed vm snapshot for different model families? Cost/ops tradeoffs?
- Are clients sending retry storms we can detect and dampen at the ingress? (has anyone seen retried HTTP 5xx patterns from this customer?)
- Get SRE signoff for changing down_stabilization default across dedicated pools (reach out to Priya).
- Explore integration with optimizer: can we precompile kernels at image build for top 10 models across pools? What is CI time & image size impact?

Action items (short):
- [ ] Run synthetic triangular ramp tests against staging-dedicated-3 (Diego)
- [ ] Add telemetry for kernel compile + kv warm events (Maya)
- [ ] Draft small autoscaler flags PR: derivative-threshold, down-stabilization override per-pool (me)
- [ ] Reproduce EBUSY GPU cleanup on test node and attach driver logs to JIRA-INF-4291 (SRE)

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc minimal and copy key findings to confluence once we have repeatable tests.
- When trying warm snapshots, start with small quantized models (q4/q8) to control memory footprint.

References / links pasted:
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/812
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INF-4291
- Quick viz: $MONITOR/dash/pool-gpu-dedicated-6/warmup

End of scratchpad.
